args.description: Schedule a call to discuss automation of ops approvals.

The decision was made to pursue this lead due to their significant company size of 450 employees and their status as a decision-maker. In the CRM, Priya's contact status was updated to "qualified," and a task was created to schedule a call to discuss their needs further.

args.description: Respond to Sam regarding the free plan request.

In the CRM, Sam's status was updated to "disqualified," and a task was created to respond to his request by November 1, 2026.

Priya Sharma is the CTO of Acme Robotics, a 450‑person manufacturing company that has already approved budget to automate its operations approvals this quarter. After confirming the company’s size, industry, and Priya’s decision‑maker role, the agent decided to pursue the lead because of the high intent and ready budget. The CRM was updated to set Priya’s contact status to **qualified**.

Jonas Weber is the IT Manager at Acme Robotics, a 450‑employee manufacturing firm, and he’s requesting pricing for roughly 200 seats with a decision expected this month. After confirming his role, company details, and the high‑intent request, the agent marked the lead as “qualified” and will pursue the opportunity. The CRM was updated to change Jonas’s contact status from “new” to “qualified.”

Mei Lin, Head of Operations at Globex Logistics, reached out because their warehouse‑approval process is chaotic and she wants to see a demo. After confirming the company details and her role as a decision influencer, the agent marked the lead as qualified and will move forward with a demo. The CRM was updated to change Mei Lin’s contact status from “new” to “qualified.”

Sam Ortiz, the Founder of TinyCo Studio (a 4‑person design studio), asked if they could receive a free plan forever. The agent rejected the lead because the company is far below the minimum size threshold, has no clear business need or budget, and is requesting a free, not paid, solution. The CRM was updated to set Sam’s contact status to **disqualified**.

Ada Park is the Head of Operations at Initech, a 300‑employee software company. After reviewing the lead, the agent decided to **pursue** the opportunity because Ada is a decision‑maker who is exploring options for next year, albeit with low urgency. No changes were made to the CRM for this lead.

Lena Fox is the VP of Operations at Umbrella Health, a 5,000‑employee healthcare organization, and she’s looking to automate approval workflows across the company’s clinics. After confirming her role, industry fit, and clear automation need, the agent decided to pursue the lead. The CRM was updated by creating a new contact record for Lena Fox (ID 5) with her name, title, email, and company details.

Omar Haddad is the Director of IT at Globex Logistics, a 1,200‑employee logistics company. After confirming his role and company details, the agent decided to pursue the lead, noting that his position makes him a key decision‑maker and the logistics industry aligns with our target market. The CRM was updated by creating a new contact record for Omar (ID 5) with his name, email, title, and company.

Raj Patel is the CTO of Hooli Freight, a logistics company with about 800 employees that wants to automate dispatch approvals next quarter. After confirming the lead’s fit—size, industry and decision‑maker role—and the clear need and timeline, the sales team decided to pursue the opportunity. The CRM was updated by creating a new contact record (ID 5) for Raj Patel with his name, email, title and company information.

Richard, the CEO of Pied Piper (12‑employee software startup), reached out expressing interest in our product for his team. After enriching the company data we determined the firm is below our target size and lacks budget or timeline details, so the decision is to **not pursue** this lead. No changes were made to the CRM record.

Tom is a student working on a thesis about CRMs and reached out via email (tom.k@gmail.com). After reviewing the lead, the agent decided to reject it because the contact is not a business decision‑maker, provides no company information, and shows no purchasing intent or budget. No updates or entries were made in the CRM for this lead.

Nina (nina.r@gmail.com) reached out looking for a junior developer position at our company. After reviewing the inquiry, the sales team decided to reject the lead because she is a job seeker rather than a decision‑maker or a potential buyer of our workflow‑automation software. The lead does not represent a B2B sales opportunity, so no action was taken in the CRM and no record was created or updated.

Mark from GrowthLeads (mark@growthleads.example) reached out with a cold pitch to sell B2B lead lists. After reviewing the lead, the sales team decided to reject the inquiry because the sender is offering a service rather than seeking one, shows no buying intent, and lacks a decision‑maker role relevant to our workflow‑automation needs. No existing contact was found in the CRM, and consequently no record was added or updated.
